subject: Estoicismo

learner_context.prior_exposure: informal only (social media excerpts, aware Marco Aurélio wrote 'Meditações'), no formal reading of primary texts

confirmed_competencies: Intuitive grasp of the core idea behind the 'dicotomia do controle' (separating what is within one's control from what is not)
Able to apply that idea to a plausible everyday scenario (traffic delay) with a coherent, correct Stoic-style response
knowledge_gaps: No familiarity with primary texts or authors beyond recognizing Marco Aurélio's 'Meditações' by name
No exposure to Sêneca or Epicteto or their specific contributions
No formal vocabulary or framework for Stoic ethics beyond the dichotomy of control (e.g. cardinal virtues, Stoic logic/physics, oikeiosis, the role of virtue as the sole good)
No knowledge of historical context or the development of the Stoic school

recommended_starting_depth.notes: Learner has no formal exposure to Stoicism but already holds a correct informal intuition about the dichotomy of control and can apply it. The path should start from first principles (history, key authors, foundational vocabulary) rather than re-teaching the dichotomy of control from scratch, while still formalizing and deepening that concept early on.

material_caveats: Evidence is based on a short, bounded diagnostic (3 questions) focused on prior exposure, conceptual understanding and one applied scenario; broader curriculum gaps (e.g. Stoic physics/logic, other philosophers) are expected to be covered as regular curriculum topics rather than further diagnostic probing.
